pricing.disclaimer: pricing: fixture-catalog · v0.1.0-illustrative · captured 2026-08-25 · illustrative list prices, not authoritative · not verified against an authoritative source
limitations: Rates are approximate and unverified. They are suitable for demonstrating the tool and for deterministic tests, and for nothing else.

On-demand list prices only. Excludes Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, enterprise discount programmes, credits, taxes and support charges, so the effective price an account actually pays is normally lower.
Single region. A rate requested for any region other than us-east-1 resolves to PriceNotFound and is reported as UNKNOWN rather than approximated.
Coverage is limited to the resource types listed below; anything else produces a visible UNKNOWN component.
Tiered pricing is represented at a single rate. Where real pricing steps down with volume, these figures correspond to the first tier and therefore overstate cost at high volume.

recommendations.title: NatEip is charged while allocated, attached or not
recommendations.detail: Every public IPv4 address carries an hourly charge from the moment it is allocated. An address kept for a machine that no longer exists costs the same as one in active use.
recommendations.condition: Applies only if the address is not required. A stable address referenced by DNS, an allowlist held by a third party, or a firewall rule elsewhere is doing a job that releasing it would break.

evidence.description: Elastic IP declared in this stack

recommendations.title: NatGateway is charged by the hour whether or not traffic flows
recommendations.detail: A NAT Gateway accrues an hourly charge for as long as it exists, plus a per-gigabyte charge for what passes through it. VPC gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB carry neither.
recommendations.condition: Applies only if the traffic through this gateway is destined for S3 and DynamoDB alone. If anything behind it reaches the public internet, or any AWS service without a gateway endpoint, the gateway is doing work endpoints cannot. Check the flow logs before acting.

evidence.description: NAT Gateway declared in this stack

recommendations.title: ApplicationServer runs continuously in development
recommendations.detail: Non-production compute is often idle outside working hours. A schedule in the usage profile changes what this tool assumes; it does not change what runs. Stopping the instance is what changes the bill.
recommendations.condition: Applies only if the workload tolerates being stopped. Anything holding state in instance storage, running a long batch, or serving a shared environment other teams depend on does not.
